title: DreamCo Model Capability and Ownership Bootcamp
purpose: Teach learners to evaluate model claims, reproduce useful capabilities, build model-powered products, and produce an independently evaluated model package.
principles: A video, model card, demo, or vendor claim is a hypothesis, not proof that DreamCo can perform the task.
Every desired capability maps to an implementation route, reproducible acceptance test, safety test, and evidence record.
Provider-specific capabilities are adapter features; model-native capabilities and platform tools must be distinguished.
A course completion certificate records demonstrated skills and does not guarantee a model will equal or exceed another model.
Learners own original course work and authorized datasets; third-party model and dataset licenses remain in force.

capability_families.description: Language understanding, generation, instruction following and multilingual tasks
Structured reasoning, decomposition, planning, uncertainty and verification
Code generation, repository navigation, debugging, tests, pull-request review and bounded repair
Image understanding, OCR, visual question answering and image-grounded reasoning
Speech recognition, diarization where supported, speech generation and voice interaction
Video understanding, temporal event extraction and audio-video alignment
Image generation, controlled edits, composition and asset production
Original music/audio generation and editing where licensed tools support it
Typed tool selection, argument validation, retries, idempotency and result verification
Browser navigation and GUI control with permissions, checkpoints and user confirmation
API authentication, MCP discovery, scoped permissions, secrets handling and connector health
Document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, citations and freshness
User-controlled memory, retrieval, correction, deletion workflows and privacy boundaries
SQL, Python analysis, data quality, metrics, charts and reproducible reports
Multi-step orchestration, delegation, durable state, approval gates and recovery
Schema-constrained JSON, validation, extraction and reliable file generation
Streaming interaction, latency budgets, interruption and graceful degradation
Perception, localization, manipulation, navigation, human-robot interaction and safe actuation
Pretraining concepts, fine-tuning, adapters, distillation, quantization and deployment
Prompt injection defense, data boundaries, access control, auditability and incident response

course_modules.title: Model and capability literacy
outcomes: separate model-native skills from tools and hosted services
read model cards, licenses, context limits and modality constraints
build a capability claim register

course_modules.title: Hallucination, uncertainty and verification
outcomes: identify unsupported claims and fabricated citations
use retrieval, tools and independent checks
express uncertainty and abstain when evidence is insufficient
measure calibration and error severity

course_modules.title: Human, AI and robot teamwork
outcomes: map tasks by human strengths, model strengths and robot strengths
design handoffs and escalation
keep humans responsible for authority-sensitive decisions
identify tasks needing a robot, assistive device or no automation

course_modules.title: Reproduce capabilities from model demonstrations
outcomes: turn a capability claim into a test specification
select local, hosted or hybrid implementations
build adapters and evaluate equivalent user outcomes
record gaps instead of claiming parity

course_modules.title: Agents, tools, APIs and MCP
outcomes: build permission-scoped tool integrations
add retries, observability and failure recovery
test prompt injection and unsafe side effects

course_modules.title: Multimodal systems
outcomes: build image, audio, video and structured-data workflows
measure modality-specific quality and latency
use human review for ambiguous high-impact outputs

course_modules.title: Retrieval, memory and data systems
outcomes: build document and vector retrieval pipelines
evaluate relevance, citation faithfulness and freshness
apply privacy-aware memory controls

course_modules.title: Embodied AI and robotics
outcomes: build simulation-first perception and control labs
define force, speed, workspace and emergency-stop limits
validate supervised hardware trials before actuation

course_modules.title: Build and own a model
outcomes: choose from API wrapper, local model, adapter fine-tune or training from scratch
prepare authorized datasets and evaluation splits
train or adapt only when compute, rights and approvals exist
export, version, benchmark and document a model artifact

course_modules.title: Capstone, deployment and maintenance
outcomes: ship a working product with tests and monitoring
publish a model card and limitations
demonstrate rollback, cost controls and learner ownership boundaries

learner_model_paths.label: Build a product using an existing model
learner_model_paths.result: A deployable application with model/provider adapters; not a newly trained model.

learner_model_paths.label: Package and run a local open-weight model
learner_model_paths.result: A configured local model package subject to its license and hardware limits.

learner_model_paths.label: Fine-tune or adapt a base model
learner_model_paths.result: A versioned adapter or merged checkpoint only after dataset rights, compute, and evaluation gates pass.

learner_model_paths.label: Train a small model from scratch
learner_model_paths.result: A new checkpoint whose capability is bounded by data, architecture, compute and measured results.

parity_policy.rule: Never infer parity from a course, marketing page, benchmark score, or successful single example. Report capability-by-capability results and unsupported features.

ownership_and_completion.ownership_note: Learners retain rights to their original work and eligible trained artifacts; base-model, dataset, software, and hosted-service licenses and terms still apply.
no_guarantees: not guaranteed to match a frontier model
not guaranteed to run on every device
not a substitute for regulated professional authorization

ai_strengths: rapid synthesis across large text collections
robot_strengths: moving objects and inspecting physical spaces
assisting with mobility or hazardous repetitive tasks when properly designed
shared_tasks: inspection with robot sensing and AI summarization
accessible interfaces combining voice, vision and controls
human-supervised automation with safe stop and recovery
hard_limits: AI systems do not have human lived experience or moral/legal accountability
robots cannot safely act outside their tested operating envelope
humans cannot reliably perform some high-volume computation or continuous monitoring without tools
all participants have failure modes; allocate work by evidence, not hype

rights_and_privacy.curriculum: DreamCo-authored explanations, examples, exercises and assessments; do not reproduce third-party course wording or imply third-party endorsement.
rights_and_privacy.sources: Keep private provenance and license records for every external reference, asset, dataset and model.
rights_and_privacy.training: Buddy has standing authorization to learn from original DreamCo-owned Bootcamp materials without repeated per-asset consent prompts. External materials, learner submissions, customer data, personal data, and third-party licensed works remain governed by their own applicable permissions and privacy settings.
rights_and_privacy.secrets: Never store credentials in lesson content, task examples, public reports or model datasets.

first_party_bootcamp_learning.standing_authorization: DreamCo authorizes Buddy to learn from, index, retrieve, summarize, evaluate, and use for internal model-training experiments all original DreamCo-authored Bootcamp curriculum assets that DreamCo owns or has authority to license.
eligibility_requirements: asset contains no unlicensed third-party text, media, code, dataset, or personal data
asset is not learner-submitted content unless that learner's applicable terms explicitly grant the required use
separate_controls: privacy and personal-data safeguards still apply
security-sensitive secrets and credentials must be excluded
safety restrictions and dataset quality checks still apply
external third-party materials retain their own license and permission conditions
customer work and learner submissions are not automatically included in DreamCo model training
first_party_bootcamp_learning.customer_model_training: A customer's course content may be used for that customer's model only within the permissions and settings the customer selects; it is not pooled into DreamCo shared training by default.
